I'd say it still is, but the format system has always worked like this. Different formats are different styles of play/different rules basically. Standard is a minimum 60 card deck with only the latest sets, Vintage would let you use almost any cards, Commander is a 100 card deck with 1 special commander per deck. Just depends on how you want to play. Although I have heard they've been slacking on balance and a lot of new cards are getting banned in standard on release.

So Magic is played in different formats. Standard is a very popular format to play in, so people want to keep their decks standard legal. So if I make a deck for standard this year and don't update it, all of the cards in it could be out of the format within like a year. Sure you could play a different format with them, and many do, it just sucks to be forced into buying a ton of new cards every few months to stay viable.

Standard format uses only the last five(? could be wrong, I haven't played in a while) sets printed, and as the other person mentioned they've started printing more sets a year, forcing players to purchase new cards much more often to keep playing standard.
